text.p: Italian debt markets slumped into the red in the afternoon session and stayed there to the close of trade, despite strength on Bunds and Treasuries.
Brokers cited investors unwinding long positions on futures and buying back cash as well as a sell-off at the short end at the very end of the day.

The March future on LIFFE was 49 basis points down at 130.33 while the November 2006 Btp closed at 19 basis points down at 104.18 and was yielding 7.27 percent, with the spread over the 10-year Bund 147 basis points. The most traded July 2006 was 36 basis points down at 109.90.

The lira failed to make much headway from the 983 per mark area seen on Wednesday despite a comment from Prime Minister Romano Prodi that he had been misunderstood when he had been reported as saying the lira was overvalued against the mark.

One broker at a large U.S. bank said the market had lost interest in Btps for now. Others said the afternoon selling came from U.S. funds, while others again said there was arbitrage selling on Btp futures in favour of UK gilt futures.
Brokers also noted while there had been no development today of the debate of Italy's prospects for being in the first wave of European monetary union, it was in everybody's minds.
"It's a delicate moment for Italian markets. The debate on entering EMU is hotting up even if there aren't any new developments for tipping the balance one way or the other," a dealer said.
